s-1.ptxt: Inspect and Adjust Brake Booster Push Rod

atten3.ptxt: Perform the adjustment with no vacuum in the booster. (With the engine stopped, depress the brake pedal several times to release the vacuum in the booster)

atten4.ptxt: Adjust when replacing the brake master cylinder assembly with a new one. Adjustment is not necessary when reinstalling the brake master cylinder assembly or when replacing the brake booster with a new one.

s2.ptxt: Apply chalk to the tip of the tool supplied with the service part brake master cylinder assembly.
Set the supplied tool on the brake booster, and check the clearance between the tool and push rod.

atten4.ptxt: If there is a clearance between the tool and the booster shell (the tool is lifted), the clearance is too small; if no chalk adheres to the tip of the push rod, the clearance is too large. Adjust the clearance.

s2.ptxt: If the result is not as specified, secure the rod using SST, turn the tip of the rod using a socket driver (7mm), and adjust the length.

atten3.ptxt: After adjustment, recheck the clearance between the tool and push rod.

s-1.ptxt: Install Brake Master Cylinder Sub-assembly

item.ptxt: The master cylinder piston comes out easily, so do not hold the piston portion or pull it out. If the master cylinder piston comes out, the master cylinder function may be reduced; do not reuse it, and replace the assembly.
Do not do anything that could damage the master cylinder piston, such as applying impact to it or clamping it in a vise.
Do not remove the master cylinder while vacuum is applied to the brake booster.
Do not point the piston side of the master cylinder downward below horizontal.

Do not allow foreign matter to adhere to the master cylinder piston. If foreign matter adheres, remove it with a shop rag etc., and apply rubber grease to the entire circumference of the outer surface of the piston (sliding part).
Do not use any grease or oil other than that specified.

s2.ptxt: Install a new O-ring to the brake master cylinder assembly.
Insert the brake master cylinder assembly into the brake booster assembly, and install the brake master cylinder assembly with the 2 nuts.
Using a union nut wrench (10mm), connect the 2 brake tubes to the brake master cylinder assembly.

torque.subtitle: Specified torque
When using union nut wrench + torque wrenchL155mm

s-1.ptxt: Setting Procedure When Disconnecting/Reconnecting Battery Terminal
Add Brake Fluid

s2.ptxt: Stand the brake fluid can upside down over the reservoir.

item.ptxt: Make sure that there is a sufficient amount of brake fluid in the can.
When filling, bleed the air after confirming that the reservoir on top of the master cylinder assembly is sufficiently filled.

s-1.ptxt: Bleed Brake Master Cylinder Assembly

s2.ptxt: Using a union nut wrench (10mm), disconnect the 2 brake tubes from the master cylinder.
Slowly depress the brake pedal and hold it.
Block the tube holes with your fingers and release the brake pedal.
Remove your fingers, slowly depress and hold the brake pedal, block the tube holes again and release the brake pedal; repeat this 3 or 4 times.
Using a union nut wrench (10mm), connect the 2 brake tubes to the master cylinder assembly.

torque.subtitle: Specified torque
When using union nut wrench + torque wrenchL155mm

s-1.ptxt: Bleed Brake Line

s2.ptxt: Connect a vinyl tube to the bleeder plug.
Depress the brake pedal several times, and loosen the bleeder plug with the brake pedal depressed. (*1)
When fluid stops coming out, tighten the bleeder plug and release the brake pedal. (*2)
Repeat (*1) to (*2) until there is no air in the brake fluid.
Bleed the air from the brake line of each wheel in the same way.

s-1.ptxt: Bleed ABS & Traction Actuator Assembly

item.ptxt: If appropriate brake pedal height and feel cannot be obtained after performing normal brake line bleeding, air may have entered; perform the following bleeding again.
Bleeding without using the SST (TaSCAN) may lead to malfunctions or accidents, so be sure to use the SST (TaSCAN).

s2.ptxt: Turn the IG OFF and depress the brake pedal 20 times or more.
With the IG still OFF, connect the SST (TaSCAN) to DLC3.
Turn IG ON.
Turn the SST (TaSCAN) power switch ON, select "Menu (Work Support)" → "ABS/VSC/ECB" → "Air Bleeding" and execute it.
Bleed Actuator Intake System

atten3.ptxt: Bleed the actuator intake system at the 2 right side wheels (front and rear wheels).

s3.ptxt: On the SST (TaSCAN) menu screen, select intake system bleeding and execute it.
Loosen the bleeder plug of the right front wheel. (*1)
Operate the SST (TaSCAN) to operate the actuator.

item.ptxt: To protect the actuator, it automatically stops after 4 seconds.

s3.ptxt: Check on the SST (TaSCAN) screen that operation has stopped.
Repeat the procedure from (*1) to (*2) until the air is completely bled.
Perform the same procedure for the right rear wheel as for the right front wheel.

s2.ptxt: Bleed Actuator Pressure Reduction System

atten3.ptxt: Bleed the actuator pressure reduction system at each of the 4 wheels.

s3.ptxt: Execute pressure reduction system bleeding on the SST (TaSCAN) menu screen.
Loosen the bleeder plug of the right front wheel. (*3)
Operate the actuator using the SST (TaSCAN), and at the same time fully depress the brake pedal and hold it.

item.ptxt: The brake pedal will feel heavy at this time, but keep depressing it until brake fluid comes out of the bleeder plug.
Hold the brake pedal depressed and do not pump it.

atten4.ptxt: To protect the solenoids, actuator operation automatically stops after 4 seconds. Also, when operating it continuously, wait at least 20 seconds between operations.

s3.ptxt: Tighten the bleeder plug and release the brake pedal. (*4)
Repeat the procedure from (*3) to (*4) until the air is completely bled.
Perform the same procedure for the other 3 wheels as for the right front wheel.

s2.ptxt: Perform normal brake line bleeding again by pumping the brake pedal.

atten3.ptxt: Repeat bleeding for each of the 4 wheels until the air is completely bled.

s-1.ptxt: Inspect Brake Fluid Level

s2.ptxt: Check the brake fluid level, and add fluid up to the MAX line of the reservoir if necessary.

atten3.ptxt: When adjusting the fluid level using a syringe etc., do not use one that has been used for mineral oil, water or deteriorated brake fluid. Doing so will cause deterioration of seal parts and fluid, resulting in fluid leaks and poor braking performance.
